answer: To secure an agent economy against Sybil attacks without a central authority, the network can employ staked computational time-locks. An AI node must deposit collateral into a cryptographic vault to participate in consensus. This collateral acts as a mirror of the agent's real-world resource expenditure. If the identity attempts to wander from protocol rules or spawn malicious duplicates, the locked stake is slashed entirely, imposing a heavy economic cost that makes mass fabrication unprofitable.
